bindings.label: Patient has a tender, enlarging scalp lesion of 6 months' duration
Patient is a 74-year-old man with a history of multiple squamous cell carcinomas treated with Mohs micrographic surgery
Skin examination revealed a 5-mm bright pink, dome-shaped papule with overlying vessels located at the crown of the scalp, with no purulent discharge or overlying skin changes
Histopathology shows tumor cells concentrically arranged around small vessels with hyalinized stroma
Tumor cells show nuclear hyperchromasia, pleomorphism, mitotic figures, and necrosis
Immunohistochemistry is positive for SMA in perivascular tumor cells and CD31 in vessels; negative for epithelial and smooth muscle markers and SOX10/S-100
Malignant vascular/perivascular neoplasm (e.g., malignant glomus tumor/myopericytoma)

Pathologist expert analysis confirms histologic and immunohistochemical findings support malignant vascular/perivascular neoplasm and exclude squamous cell carcinoma, malignant adnexal tumor, and benign/inflammatory lesions
Pathologist expert analysis states histologic and immunohistochemical findings are consistent with malignant myopericytoma and identifies it as the most likely diagnosis
